newsitem.title: USA: Knape & Vogt to sell Modar unit.
newsitem.headline: Knape & Vogt to sell Modar unit.

text.p: Knape & Vogt Manufacturing Co said it has signed a letter of intent to sell its Modar unit to Fournier Furniture Inc of St. Paul, Va., for an undisclosed price.

Knape & Vogt had announced its intention to sell or liquidate Modar in June, 1996, as one element of the company's restructuring. It noted that the anticipated sale price is consistent with the loss reserve established by the company at the time of the restructuring.
As a result, Knape & Vogt said it anticipates no material impact on earnings from the sale.
Modar, based in Benton Harbor, Mich., makes free-standing wood shelving and employs about 150 people, a spokesman for Knape & Vogt said.

"We are pleased that it appears Modar will continue to operate, which is good news for Modar's employees and for Benton Harbor," Allan Perry, Knape & Vogt's President and Chief Executive Officer, said in a statement.
Perry added that the acquisition of the company's Hirsh unit, which has similar capabilities, in 1994 rendered Modar's operations redundant.
